clue.text: Urge Arthur to extract the soil

indicators.note: to extract is to draw something out, here a run of letters pulled from inside the two words Urge Arthur

explanation.surface: Someone is pressing a man called Arthur to dig out the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extract' signals a run of letters drawn from inside 'Urge Arthur', across the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the ordinary word for the ground's soil, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Regard leading batsman as something amazing

parts.note: to regard is to look at, to eye
in cricket the opener is the batsman who goes in first

explanation.surface: A spectator watches a top-order cricketer and finds him a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsmen bat first, so a 'leading batsman' is an opener.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprising revelation that opens one's eyes, an idiom for anything astonishing.

clue.text: Field-work in which soldiers have little faith

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
doubt is a lack of belief

explanation.surface: A fortification is manned by troops who lack confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a temporary outlying fortification thrown up in the field, a military earthwork.

clue.text: Sounds like a brave greeting from a cabinet minister

indicators.note: the clue says the greeting is what is heard when the name is spoken

parts.note: 'how' is the stock greeting given to a Native American warrior (a brave) in old westerns

explanation.surface: A government minister greets people like a warrior in a western.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Howe was a senior British Cabinet minister under Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Geoffrey Howe served as Chancellor and Foreign Secretary in Thatcher's Cabinet.

clue.text: Last month I got married at 10 percent discount

parts.note: December, abbreviated Dec, is the last month of the year
mated means paired off, coupled

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a December wedding and a sale where everything was a tenth off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition uses the original Roman sense: to decimate was to kill one soldier in every ten, so a decimated thing has lost a tenth.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, reduced by one tenth, as in the Roman punishment of killing every tenth man.

clue.text: He's not to cease making Welsh rarebit

indicators.note: making here means producing something new out of the letters supplied before it

parts.note: the possessive apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: Someone vows never to stop preparing a Welsh cheese dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' turns the letters of HE'S NOT TO CEASE into the snack.
explanation.definitionFit: Welsh rarebit is a dish of melted, seasoned cheese on toasted bread.

clue.text: Complaint of a hungry fellow

parts.note: a starving man grumbles, and the clue asks for the word for that grumble; one reading also sees nothing (O) inside a man

explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a low grumble or complaint, the sound an empty stomach prompts.

clue.text: Sally gets accommodation in chic market-town

indicators.note: to be accommodated in something is to be housed within it, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: the ton is an old word for fashionable society, chic style
Aunt Sally is a pub game and a figure set up to be knocked down

explanation.surface: A taunt is lodged somewhere fashionable in a country town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a taunt (a sally is a witty jibe), but it gives AUNT, from Aunt Sally, a traditional British pub throwing game. TON is old slang for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunton is the county town of Somerset, a long-established market centre.

clue.text: Fancy a tot being full of energy

indicators.note: something full of a thing holds it inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a lively toddler, or a small drink with a kick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' suggests a child but means a small measure of spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy something is to imagine it or wish for it, as one does in a reverie.

clue.text: Left money to meet the final instalment

definitions.text: Left money to meet the final instalment

parts.words: Left money to meet the final instalment
parts.note: the clue reads as a bequest made to clear a last payment, while describing someone who was given funds by will, with END and OWED in the picture too

explanation.definitionFit: To be given an income or bequest by someone's will is to be so provided for.

clue.text: Attending an aerobics class in prison

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: performing a limbering exercise, and serving a jail sentence.

clue.text: Strangely rare use of blue pen oil

indicators.note: strangely says the letters that follow appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: An editor is unusually sparing with the censor's blue pencil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' reworks RARE USE. An editor's blue pencil is used to strike text out.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue pencil is the editor's tool for crossing out text, so it stands for deletion.

clue.text: Prize fruit

definitions.meaning: a ... job or role is a choice, much-sought one

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a choice, coveted thing (a plum post) and the purple stone fruit.

clue.text: Get up about noon and wash

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: to get up is to rise

explanation.surface: A late riser gets out of bed at midday and showers.
explanation.definitionFit: To rinse is to wash lightly in clean water.

clue.text: Check the root

definitions.meaning: to ... a flow is to stop or check it
the ... of a word is its base form or root

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to halt a flow, and the base of a word or plant shoot.

clue.text: Self-righteous act put on by an Eastern chef, maybe

definitions.text: put on by an Eastern chef, maybe

parts.note: pi is British slang short for pious, sanctimonious
an act of parliament is a law

explanation.surface: A preachy piece of legislation is enforced by a cook from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes a dish an Eastern cook might serve up.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilaw (pilaf) is a spiced rice dish of the Middle East and Asia, something a cook would serve.

clue.text: Lesson for Frenchman taking an examination

parts.note: M, short for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A man from France sits a test to learn something.
explanation.definitionFit: The moral of a story is the lesson it teaches.

clue.text: Lack of information about whether VAT and service are included

definitions.meaning: having no clues or facts to work from

definitions.text: whether VAT and service are included
definitions.meaning: read literally, nothing extra is to be added on top of the bill

explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, no evidence to act on; literally, no tax or tip to be added to a bill.

clue.text: Advocate alcohol-free liquor in a rural retreat

parts.note: to back a cause is to advocate it
water is a liquid with no alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller champions soft drinks in a quiet country spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A backwater is a quiet, isolated place untouched by progress.

clue.text: An art list can't be reproduced in America

indicators.note: to be reproduced is to be made again, here in a fresh order of letters

parts.note: the apostrophe adds no letter

explanation.surface: A list of artworks cannot be copied over in the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be reproduced' rearranges AN ART LIST CANT. From Britain, America lies across the Atlantic.
explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, America is across the ocean, so anything there is over the Atlantic.

clue.text: Butter with a pungent taste presents a puzzle

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour
a ram is a butter, an animal that butts

explanation.surface: Dairy butter with a sharp flavour is puzzling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the spread: a ram butts, so it is a butter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese dissection puzzle of seven pieces forming shapes.

clue.text: Thing to be resolved this evening

indicators.note: something resolved is worked out or broken down, so these letters settle into a new order

explanation.surface: There is a matter that must be settled before the night is out.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight means during the coming evening or night of today.

clue.text: Admit one's inability to write jargon

explanation.walkthrough: The first sense is spelt with an apostrophe (can't), the second without.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a contraction of cannot, and the private slang of a trade or group.

clue.text: Police take a key from the undergrowth

parts.note: cops is slang for police officers
E is one of the musical keys

explanation.surface: Officers seize a key found in the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket of trees and shrubs, a patch of brushwood.

clue.text: The best sort of medicament

definitions.meaning: the ... of the crop is the finest part
an ointment applied to the skin

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the pick or elite of a group, and a soothing lotion for the skin.

clue.text: Cocaine commonly found in the South at present

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
now means at this moment

explanation.surface: Drugs are said to be widespread in the southern region these days.
explanation.definitionFit: In street slang cocaine is called this, from its white powder.

clue.text: What slow bowlers aim to do in a brieftour

definitions.text: What slow bowlers aim to do
definitions.meaning: slow bowlers in cricket try to make the ball turn off the pitch
a short trip out, as in a quick drive in the car

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, slow bowlers rely on turning the ball rather than pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: imparting turn to a cricket ball, and a short pleasure trip in a car.

clue.text: High-ranking officer goes to work in animal shelter

parts.note: CO, a commanding officer
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A senior officer starts work at the animal sanctuary.
explanation.definitionFit: A coop is a cage or pen for poultry or small animals.

clue.text: Defence provided by a regimental mascot

parts.note: a Para is a soldier of the Parachute Regiment
a regimental mascot is a kept animal, a pet

explanation.surface: An army unit's animal mascot is put forward as protection.
explanation.walkthrough: A Para is a member of Britain's Parachute Regiment.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a protective wall or bank shielding troops from enemy fire.

clue.text: Thursday should be considered

parts.note: ought means should

explanation.surface: A suggestion that Thursday deserves to be taken into account.
explanation.definitionFit: Thought, as a past participle, means mulled over, reflected upon.

clue.text: Cook lent me ham and cheese

indicators.note: to cook figures is to falsify or rework them, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to prepare a ham and cheese dish from what someone lent.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmenthal is a Swiss hard cheese with large holes.

clue.text: Minced liver recipe from a Victorian essayist

parts.note: pâté is a paste of minced liver
R, from Latin recipe, the abbreviation on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A recipe for liver pâté comes from a nineteenth-century writer.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the old prescription abbreviation for Latin recipe, 'take'.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Pater was a Victorian critic and essayist on Renaissance art.
